name: User
rationale: Authenticated actors share a common user identity for login and session-bound authorization.
plain_english_summary: A person who can authenticate to iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: User__mid
rationale: MID is the login identifier and is assigned to some users.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical identification number used for login.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled credentials as a separate resource, but MID is also a stable user identifier.

name: User__password
rationale: Password is part of authentication and credential secrecy requirements.
plain_english_summary: The user's password credential.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled only a passwordHash field, but the spec names password directly.

name: User__securityQuestion
rationale: Security question must be representable for HCP non-access requirements.
plain_english_summary: The user's account security question.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
alternatives_considered: Placed only on Patient, but the wording describes account credentials.

name: Patient
rationale: Patients are principals and resources with patient-specific privacy relationships.
plain_english_summary: A patient whose account and medical information are managed in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Patient__isActive
rationale: Deactivated patient restrictions require lifecycle state on the patient account.
plain_english_summary: Whether the patient account is active or deactivated.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system and can only be reactivated by an administrator.
alternatives_considered: Modeled status as a string enum, but the spec only distinguishes deactivated versus not.

name: Patient__designatedLhcps
rationale: DLHCP is patient-specific and must be represented as a relationship rather than a global role only.
plain_english_summary: The licensed health-care professionals this patient has designated.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
alternatives_considered: Modeled DLHCP only as a principal entity type, but the spec says designation is for that patient.

name: Patient__providerList
rationale: The patient provider list is needed for viewing and adding patient providers.
plain_english_summary: The LHCPs on the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP to the patient provider list.
alternatives_considered: Used office visits alone, but the spec separately names a provider list.

name: Patient__visitedLhcps
rationale: The patient can view LHCPs they have ever had office visits with.
plain_english_summary: LHCPs the patient has previously visited.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Derived from OfficeVisit records, but the spec directly asks to view this set.

name: HCP
rationale: HCPs are principals for patient account and medical-record actions.
plain_english_summary: A health-care professional using iTrust.
source_excerpt: Doctors and other health-care workers can obtain and share essential patient information and view aggregate patient data.

name: LHCP
rationale: Licensed HCPs have special patient-designation and administrative creation semantics.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health-care professional.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: Hospital assignment constraints require the LHCP-to-hospital relationship.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals an LHCP is assigned to.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrators create staff, assign credentials, reactivate patients, and configure inactivity limits.
plain_english_summary: An administrative user who manages accounts and system settings.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are named actor types requiring account creation and likely emergency access distinctions.
plain_english_summary: A user who responds to emergencies.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: UAP
rationale: UAP users are created by LHCPs and can access demographic and medical information.
plain_english_summary: Unlicensed assistive personnel user.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representative principals need patient-specific represented-person relationships.
plain_english_summary: A user who may act on behalf of a patient they represent.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: PersonalRepresentative__representedPatients
rationale: Representative authority is patient-specific and reused across record and access-log actions.
plain_english_summary: The patients this person is authorized to represent.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.
alternatives_considered: Flattened personal representative into a global role, but the spec says representation is for particular patients.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are named users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A public-health user account.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: LabTechnician
rationale: Lab technicians are named users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A lab technician user account.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: SoftwareTester
rationale: Software Tester is an important actor named in the slice.
plain_english_summary: A software tester user account.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are resources in LHCP assignment constraints.
plain_english_summary: A hospital from the approved hospital list.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

name: Session
rationale: Global authenticated-session lifecycle rules require a reusable session boundary for protected actions.
plain_english_summary: An authenticated login session that may expire or terminate.
source_excerpt: Authenticated sessions terminate after inactivity, logout, or closing the application.

name: Session__isActive
rationale: Authorization is disabled after session expiry, so actions need active-session state.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently active.
source_excerpt: After the inactivity limit is exceeded, authorization is disabled.
alternatives_considered: Used only an expiresAt timestamp, but the spec directly states authorization is disabled after inactivity.

name: Session__user
rationale: Protected actions need to bind the session to the requesting user.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the authenticated session.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.

name: Session__lastActivityAt
rationale: Inactivity-based termination depends on when the session was last active.
plain_english_summary: The time of the user's last activity in this session.
source_excerpt: Authenticated sessions terminate after inactivity, logout, or closing the application.

name: SystemSettings
rationale: The administrator-configured inactivity period is a system-level resource.
plain_english_summary: System-wide configurable settings for iTrust.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: SystemSettings__inactivityPeriod
rationale: Authorization expiry depends on the configured inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before authorization is disabled.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are central protected patient resources.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Own-record and represented-record access requires linking records to the patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose record this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent
alternatives_considered: Used action context only, but ownership is persistent on the record.

name: DiagnosticInformation
rationale: Diagnostic information has patient-controlled restrictions and LHCP viewing rules.
plain_english_summary: Diagnosis-related information in a patient's record.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: DiagnosticInformation__patient
rationale: Diagnosis access restrictions are controlled by the affected patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient this diagnostic information belongs to.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: DiagnosticInformation__isRestricted
rationale: Selected diagnoses can have restricted viewing.
plain_english_summary: Whether viewing this diagnosis has been restricted.
source_excerpt: For selected diagnostic information, such as mental-illness, substance-abuse, or cosmetic surgery diagnoses, the patient can restrict viewing.
alternatives_considered: Modeled diagnosis category enum, but policy needs the selected restricted state.

name: DiagnosticInformation__restrictionAllowed
rationale: An LHCP determines whether a patient is allowed to restrict a diagnosis.
plain_english_summary: Whether the patient may restrict viewing of this diagnosis.
source_excerpt: A licensed health-care professional determines whether the patient is allowed to restrict viewing of a diagnosis.

name: DiagnosticInformation__allowedViewers
rationale: The patient can choose designated LHCPs, other LHCPs, or no one for restricted diagnostic viewing.
plain_english_summary: Which LHCPs may view this restricted diagnostic information.
source_excerpt: A patient can enable designated licensed health-care professionals, other licensed health-care professionals, or no one to view restricted diagnostic information.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as a coarse visibility enum, but explicit viewer set supports patient-specific permissions.

name: PersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a separately named protected resource.
plain_english_summary: Personal health information belonging to a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: PersonalHealthInformation__patient
rationale: Access and edit rules are for a selected or represented patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient this personal health information belongs to.
source_excerpt: An HCP can enter and edit a patient's personal health records.

name: FamilyHistory
rationale: Family history is named as viewable medical information.
plain_english_summary: A patient's family medical history.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: FamilyHistory__patient
rationale: Own and represented access requires the family history owner.
plain_english_summary: The patient this family history belongs to.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent

name: Immunization
rationale: Immunizations are separately viewable and editable medical data.
plain_english_summary: A patient's immunization information.
source_excerpt: An HCP can edit historical values, immunizations, office-visit information, family history, BMI, and death status for a selected patient.

name: Immunization__patient
rationale: Immunization access and editing are scoped to a selected patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient this immunization belongs to.
source_excerpt: for a selected patient

name: OfficeVisit
rationale: Office visits are protected resources documented, edited, viewed, and surveyed.
plain_english_summary: An office visit recorded for a patient.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: OfficeVisit__patient
rationale: Office visits are for selected patients and patient-owned views.
plain_english_summary: The patient associated with the office visit.
source_excerpt: for a selected patient

name: OfficeVisit__hospital
rationale: The office-visit record includes hospital information.
plain_english_summary: The hospital where the office visit occurred.
source_excerpt: including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals

name: OfficeVisit__surveyTaken
rationale: Survey authorization depends on whether the survey has already been taken.
plain_english_summary: Whether the satisfaction survey for this office visit has already been submitted.
source_excerpt: If a patient or personal representative has not taken an office-visit satisfaction survey, they may take the survey; after the survey has been taken, they cannot take or view the previously submitted survey through that path.
alternatives_considered: Created a separate Survey resource, but the rule is tied to each office visit.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Access logs are patient-related resources that patients and representatives may view.
plain_english_summary: A record of access to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Access-log viewing is scoped to the patient or represented person.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: for themself or a represented person

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: The spec describes accessor name as part of access logs.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the information.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessorRole
rationale: The spec describes accessor role relative to the patient as logged data.
plain_english_summary: The accessor's role relative to the patient.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessedAt
rationale: The spec describes date/time as part of access logs.
plain_english_summary: When the access occurred.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: The spec describes transaction type as part of access logs.
plain_english_summary: The kind of transaction that was logged.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: ProviderDesignation
rationale: Provider designations are explicit resources for designating or undesignating patient-specific DLHCP relationships.
plain_english_summary: A record that an LHCP is designated for a patient.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: ProviderDesignation__patient
rationale: A provider designation belongs to a particular patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient who made the designation.
source_excerpt: for that patient

name: ProviderDesignation__lhcp
rationale: A provider designation names the LHCP being designated.
plain_english_summary: The LHCP designated by the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship
rationale: Personal-representative status is patient-specific and is managed as a resource.
plain_english_summary: A relationship showing that a user represents a patient.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__patient
rationale: Representative relationships are for selected patients.
plain_english_summary: The patient being represented.
source_excerpt: for a selected patient

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__representative
rationale: Representative relationships identify the registered user who represents the patient.
plain_english_summary: The user who is the patient's personal representative.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.
alternatives_considered: Typed as PersonalRepresentative only, but the spec says another registered user can be added.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Demographic information is a named resource entered and edited by UAPs.
plain_english_summary: A patient's demographic data.
source_excerpt: UAP can enter and edit demographic information, diagnosis, office visit notes, and other medical information, and can view records.

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic information is patient data and must be scoped to a patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient this demographic information belongs to.
source_excerpt: The HCP can enter a patient as a new user and can edit the patient according to the patient data format, but the patient MID cannot be edited.

name: login
